entries.title: The Legends - Day 1
entries.body:
I woke up in my old childhood room. As I woke up, I saw my sister shaking me, yelling urgently, “PETER! Wake up! Something weird is in the living room.”

I asked, “What do you mean, ‘something weird’?”

She looked at me with a serious face, saying, “Follow me,” and led me to the living room.

To my surprise, I saw something that looked like a person covered in black goo, with no eyes or mouth. Black goo. External evil!

“All right, Lily, go as quickly as you can to Mom and Dad’s room and don’t stop,” I instructed.

“Okay,” Lily responded purposefully.

When Lily left the room, it stared at me, trying to intimidate me with a blank look.

entries.title: Day 1
entries.body:
I woke up in my old childhood room. As I woke up, I saw my sister shaking me, yelling urgently, “PETER! Wake up! Something weird is in the living room.”

I asked, “What do you mean, ‘something weird’?”

She looked at me with a serious face, saying, “Follow me,” and led me to the living room.

To my surprise, I saw something that looked like a person covered in black goo, with no eyes or mouth. Black goo. External evil!

“All right, Lily, go as quickly as you can to Mom and Dad’s room and don’t stop,” I instructed.

“Okay,” Lily responded purposefully.

When Lily left the room, it stared at me, trying to intimidate me with a blank look.

entries.title: Day 2
entries.body:
From the rude awakening of this guy who was in my house uninvited, I kept staring and waited for what he would do next after my sister went away. It did also...

I knew the Black Goo was planning to kill me in the darkness. Oh, did I say kill? I meant consuming me. It ran toward me and pushed me to the ground to get the chance to do what it hoped, but instantly I moved my body away from it. It turned its head to face mine, snapping its neck, and then formed a face with no nose or eyebrows. It had sharp red teeth and eyes that both stretched to the sides of its face. It leaped to the ground, holding my neck with one arm, and with the other it held its body above mine. Then, with a mischievous smile, it started squeezing my neck slowly.

This is war!

I pushed on one of its arms, causing it to break and for its organism to fall on me with a screech of pain. The Black Goo just stopped. With its arm still on my neck, it sent some of itself onto me.

That means it's a...

entries.title: Day 3
entries.body:
That means it's a protist controlling a host. It felt slimy yet hard when climbing onto my chest, looking like a liquid shadow. It moved like, no, not moved; it glided on the ground like sloosh but still had volume. It pulled itself onto my shoulder with small things like arms, but they were more like grappling strings with a sticky and shiny texture. Not one, but millions were pulling in the direction it wanted to go.

It stretched itself to touch both sides of my body, extending to make ropes with the same texture as itself. Eventually, it had four ropes attached to the ground around me, pulling me against the ground. Nearly in the ground, I reached for the other arm of the organism and broke it. I didn’t stop there; I pulled off the arm.

Then another arm appeared. It was shaped like a samurai sword. Of course, it didn't stop there! It tried to stab me, and then I saw a bunch of light appear to come from my body. It evaporated The Black Goo and left a human with blonde hair and blue eyes.

entries.title: Day 4
entries.body:
The human looked like he hadn't eaten in years. The human looked like a man, but it was hard to tell. I knew from earlier that this person was lost, but not this lost. I didn't know.

I couldn't do anything for him because of the condition he was in, but I could do one thing: tell someone.

So I went to my parents and told them what had happened. They looked at each other with dread, as if they knew this was going to happen. They then responded, "Alright, we know this is confusing, but there is no time to explain anything. Grab Jake and take both him and Lily out of this area. When you get to your school, you'll know what to do."

So Jake, Lily, and I set out on the journey ahead.

entries.title: Day 5
entries.body:
My parents said goodbye, and I finished the fight, beginning a journey filled with questions. My mind tells me not to listen, but a force deep within my spirit urges me to keep going and bring this conflict to an end.

We run outside with a mission: to escape, to flee from the chaos and pain. It doesn't feel right. We need to fight! But we can't. We must keep running if we want to survive.

The Black Goo roars behind eating the world from a big bottomless pit that keeps growing and realizing more organisms. While ahead? There’s salvation.

entries.title: Day 6
entries.body:
There were people fighting back, with tight suits made of a flexible alloy with bright-colored lines all over them and gigantic sword-like weapons especially made for destroying the Black Goo. They seemed alien like the Black Goo, but still like humans. They were the height of a moose, but had the same shape and similar looks, only better. 

The Black Goo had the most alien look. It was the same height as the fighters. Its looks were demon-like, but not completely; it still was a humanoid. 

Then I saw every fighter do exactly what had happened when the light appeared in the fight that I had with The Black Goo.

entries.title: Day 7
entries.body:
The Black Goo evaporated, and just like what happened to me, there were humans left behind. They seemed confused at first, but then they all realized what was happening and grabbed weapons from the fighters. They became fighters themselves, starting a battle, The Battle Of Life.

Jake then looked at me with compassion and said, “Why aren’t we fighting?!”

Almost instantly, I responded, “We ca... You know what, Jake? You’re right. Let’s fight.”

Lily yelled, “No! Mom and Dad said to go to your school, not fight!”

I responded to her in a sharp voice, “Shut up.”

We all then picked up weapons and became fighters.

entries.title: Day 8
entries.body:
The weapon didn’t feel like an ordinary earthly sword; it had energy attached to it, like the feeling of The Bust of Light. It wasn’t only that. The strength in my soul and the fire in my veins surged with it. Energy coursed through my hands, and it felt powerful, like I could tear the ground out from beneath this Black Goo. I could seriously destroy this thing.

It had the shape of a sword, but its end held another blade, with a handle in the middle. The blades were like two tall, singular spikes of gray crystal that I had never seen before.

Lily felt it too, because the moment she touched that weapon, she glared at her enemy with an intense stare, a determined grin, and her head tilted forward. She looked like she was about to destroy. Then she lifted her hands, and something appeared: purple, translucent bubbles.

entries.title: Day 9
entries.body:
She spread out her hands and the bubbles released, moving towards the black goo. They lowered to where it was, and Lily allowed them to touch the black goo and pop, causing scarlet red gas to appear, blinding me.

I heard screeching.

Then it disappeared. Mysteriously, all the black goo was gone, and in their place were shriveled bodies. Just like when the burst of light evaporated the black goo. Everyone that I saw stared at Lily, astonished at what she had done. Some even spoke, "How did she do that?" or "This is impossible."

entries.title: Day 10
entries.body:
One man from the crowd, who was wearing a maroon suit jacket with a green shirt and maroon pants and a helmet that had tinted glass and metal the same color as his jacket, walked up to us and pressed the side of his helmet. He then said, "We found them."

Was he talking about us? I thought to myself as I saw something in the tinted glass covering his face that looked like words, but it was hard to tell because the glass seemed to be made where words seemed blurry to the people on the outside.

I then stared at him to see what he meant by the words he spoke. He saw me and said, "What?" "What do you mean by 'we found them'?"

"Well, we were looking for you and your siblings…"

The man pointed at the crowd behind him and continued, "...this is the group I'm referring to when I say 'we,' and look, we found you!"

entries.title: Day 11
entries.body:
“And why exactly were you looking for us?” I asked suspiciously.

“Because if we didn’t find you, The Black Goo would eat you all up and our home would also be eaten too. That wouldn’t be good, won’t it?” — talking to me like I was a baby and with a grim tone. A great combination!

I was starting to get really annoyed with this man. He was condescending and rude, but what he was saying seemed important to him, and to me it was getting interesting and funny. But it also seemed really confusing. Because I guess I was really annoyed and my brain just wanted to make things overdramatic, I yelled, “What?!” out of impulse.

“Oh, your parents might’ve not told you under such short notice…”

The way he was talking also made Jake annoyed, because the way he looked at the guy had a familiar look to it. WAIT NO! “Jake don’-”

Really fast, Jake moved as he slapped him, but the thing that was different was there were lime green streaks of light that moved with his hand, faster than I could realize. The man flew, like literally flew, away the moment before the hand hit his face. Then Jake just said, “Bro just shut up!” annoyed.

entries.title: Day 12
entries.body:
“How!?” I asked, astonished as the man landed back on the ground.

“First of all, you got some strong powers, kid,” the man said, talking to my brother. “Second of all, me and our people have powers to shape the universe, multiverse, dimensions, and so on, including your parents.”

“So all humans have superpowers?” asked Lily.

“We are not humans.”

“So why are we here?” asked Jake.

“That I will explain later, but we gotta get goin’.”

“Where?”

“To your middle school.”

We started walking again with the man and the crowd with us.

entries.title: Day 13
entries.body:
As we were walking, we all saw another group of fighters. They were wearing suits made of a dark green material, covered in lines of glowing lime-green light. The fighters were battling the black goo and winning easily.

Then I saw the most bizarre thing I'd ever seen in my lifetime. Vine-like tentacles came out of their hands while across from them, the black goo held a girl ten feet in the air with black tentacles around her neck. The fighters' tentacles reached toward the girl, trying to save her.

entries.title: Day 14
entries.body:
I turned back to see the man not looking at the scene, saying, “Come on, Peter,” not even sounding concerned. Instead, he walked the other way. Why would he do that? What about the girl’s safety? It concerned me that he didn’t even react.

I stood there looking at the man and my siblings walk further and further together with the crowd. Behind me, I heard the roar of the battle, the clashes of swords, the screeching of the black goo, and the thud of the fighters falling to the floor and dying.

So I decided to stop trying to get to safety and start fighting.

entries.title: Day 15
entries.body:
I continued watching the battle to see the best point to get in there. I focused on a man who was in the battle. He had a sword and seemed to be the main star. The warrior was slicing through black goo after black goo, together with the whole army, smiling. He was tall, just like me and everyone I knew, and he had brown hair, but before I even got a good look at his face, a black goo ran behind him and stabbed him. The warrior dropped his sword and fell face forward, giving me a chance to fight.

I walked over to him, exposing myself. I grabbed the sword and said, “Thank you,” respectfully.

entries.title: Day 16
entries.body:
When I walked over to the wounded warrior, I saw the battle stop. I mean every black goo and warrior stopped. They all focused on me, and some warriors said, "Another one," in shock. Then it started again when I picked up the sword, every warrior back in their places. But someone in the army yelled, “Everyone surround him!” loud and sharp. Everyone did what he said, but just enough so that I was protected on all sides except the front.
The black goo was different from the one I fought earlier. It had arm blades, and instead of eyes stretched to the side of its head, it had vicious eyes shaped like crystals. It was tall and had scorpion-like legs that didn’t have feet, but spikes. Yet somehow, it was all goo.

entries.title: Day 17
entries.body:
The black goo stood tall above me, and it did seem like it would be hard to beat, but it was also the only thing blocking us from getting to the girl. So I stepped back a couple of feet from the creature; thankfully, it didn’t follow me. The only things that followed me were my defenders and some black goo that they blocked. That meant I was safe to do what I wanted to do next.
I ran as hard and as fast as I could and jumped right in front of the creature, fast enough to where it couldn’t touch me. With the ground I jumped from rising below me, I leaped high enough to reach the girl and tackled her, breaking past the tentacles that bound her. Finally, I fell with the sword aimed inside the mouth of the creature, who looked at me as I fell, and stabbed it. That ended up killing it, and at the exact moment it died, the girl fell…

entries.title: Day 18
entries.body:
The girl fell from my grasp and landed on her back, knocking her unconscious.
I failed, and failed badly. She could possibly be dead, and it's all my fault. But surprisingly, everyone didn’t feel the same way. They all applauded with joy. I stood there confused as the black goo went toward the creature and it all disappeared. The man from earlier came back from where he had left with my siblings, saying “Great job, kid!” with a smile.
I looked at everyone in confusion. Why would everyone applaud when the girl I tried to save was still hurt? What just happened with the black goo? And where were my siblings? Those were the normal questions any human would have, but these people were just clapping.

entries.title: Day 19
entries.body: The people were still applauding when the man said, “It's all right, kid, you didn’t kill her.” I made the most disgusted face and yelled, “Do you think that’s all I’m about?!” Then I continued at a respectable volume, “I mean, come on, do you really think that a normal human wouldn't be confused as heck in this situation? But don’t get me wrong, I was worried about the girl… ” I turned to the girl and asked, “Are you alright?” She was standing now, and with a snooty face she said, “Yeah.” I then continued with what I was saying: “...and I appreciate the applause. But I still don’t know what’s going on or where we’re going. So can you please answer those questions before you confuse me more?” He responded, “Well…”

entries.title: Day 20
entries.body:
“Well, first, your siblings are in our safe house. Second, what we are doing is gathering the kids who have powers like you, training them in our Academy of Warriors (A.O.W. for short), and putting you out in battle. And finally, we are going to what is left of Ogymon,” responded the man, sounding sad as he said the last part.
Just then, I realized that I didn’t know his name, even though I had been arguing with him. “Sir, thank you. I am so sorry that I didn’t ask for your name.”
“Dude, you’re all good. You reacted a lot better compared to how this girl reacted. People address me as Captain Martin,” he said, looking at the girl jokingly.

entries.title: Day 21
entries.body:
The girl walked over. She looked at me wide-eyed. She was pretty, with beautiful light blue eyes and dark brown hair. But I didn’t like her because I wanted to be realistic, and the obvious factor was that I didn’t even know her.
She held out her hand to greet me and said, “Hi, I’m Layla.” I shook her hand and responded, “Nice to meet you, Layla. I’m Peter.” I loosened my grip on the handshake to let go, but she didn’t. Instead, she made intense eye contact with me and whispered, “Don’t even think about it, Peter,” saying my name sharply. “Think about what?” I said in a tough tone. “You know,” she replied, back to her normal tone.
“Alright, you two, stop romancing. It’s time to go,” said the captain, and she walked away slowly, avoiding eye contact. In response, I said, “Bruh.” From there, the journey continued.

entries.title: Day 22
entries.body:
Layla still acted like this and said nothing. When we started again, the two crowds joined into one. Then we found another situation where there was another group of fighters. This time, the kid with them was fighting with them instead of being in trouble. This repeated over and over again with other groups until we were at the school. We ended up with five groups of fighters. There were not five kids, but only two.

After the whole process, it seemed to be around 9 PM. Even though it was not even bedtime, I was tired, which was new for me.

The captain showed us around. My whole school got ruined in one night. The previous day, the building was free of this black goo. This put me in shock.

entries.title: Day 23
entries.body:
“What happened here?” I asked.

Captain Martin said, “Something happened this morning. You slept in until 12:00. While you were asleep, we came, and with us also came the black goo, which in three hours consumed your town. If we don’t…”

I decided not to listen to what he was saying, but instead, I looked around.

With us was Layla. She was still locked in to what he was saying and not focusing on anything else. But then she caught my glance at her. Instead of looking away like a normal person, she had to make a rude face, roll her eyes up, and then look back at Captain Martin.

I looked back at the surroundings. We were walking in the normal hallway with lockers on the walls. But something was different…

entries.title: Day 24
entries.body:
There were cords of what seemed to be black goo. They went out of a corroded wall and throughout the hallway. When we turned left, they still kept going. With the one I was looking at, there were others coming from different directions, but all of them seemed to be going to the same place.

Then suddenly, after another turn, I saw where the cords were going. A teenager. He had black goo on him and was muttering something.

The captain told Layla and me to stop. So we did. He walked to the teenager cautiously and asked, “Are you okay?”

Instead of answering, the teenager stopped muttering, stood up, and slowly walked toward Layla and me.

entries.title: Day 25
entries.body:
The teenager still said nothing, but he did stare, which was a good start. Layla whispered, “Not yet.” It was the first time she had talked to me normally. I wasn’t even sure if this guy was human.

After staring into my eyes for a moment, he punched me across the face. Surprisingly, I did not retaliate.

Layla looked me in the eyes to give me the signal. But when I tried to defend myself after this guy’s one shot, I couldn’t. I was tied in something, and so was the teenager. I knew we were screwed.

I looked down, and I was tangled in vines.

entries.title: Day 26
entries.body:
Layla looked at me, barely laughing. “I got this.”

I joined in with the fun. “Well, obviously!”

She was not that serious. At least she can have fun, but this was not the situation to make fun of. We could possibly die at any second, either from this guy or from something unknown.

I think this was the first time I was serious in my whole life of 12 years. But the weird thing was, no one else was as serious as me. Also, I knew I should feel the same way as them because they had more experience than me.

entries.title: Day 27
entries.body:
What’s going on?!” I asked. They started to laugh, and then the captain said, “Why wouldn’t we laugh?” The teenager said, “I will kill both of you, your family, and everyone you know all at once.” Then Layla said, “So cute, he thinks he can kill us,” and put her hat on his head to call him short. We were all tall compared to him; he was about five feet.
“Alright, let’s get this guy to the healing center,” said the captain. We changed course and continued walking, still not getting answers to any of the questions I asked.

entries.title: Day 28
entries.body:
Layla then grew vines out of her hands and wrapped them around his torso. They continued to grow, not around the rest of his body, but toward me. I stepped back, and they kept coming. I slowly continued to back up, thinking I was in the way. They kept extending, so I asked, “What are you doing, Layla?” Still extending the vines toward me, she responded, “Taking you to the base.”
“Why are you trying to trap me?” I asked.
“Safety precautions.”
Layla detached the part of the vine wrapped around the guy and somehow fused the vine to itself, trapping him, all while the original vine extended, rebuilding the cells that were attached to the other part. Then Captain Martin took the teenager away, leaving me and her alone.

entries.title: Day 29
entries.body:
“I am safe by myself, thank you though,” I said, getting ready to protect myself from the grasp of the vine. Layla then looked at me with a dumbfounded face. What smart alec move was she going to make next? She responded, “Then what do you call that ‘boy saves girl’ move out there?”
“Saving your butt!” I said, stating my case.
She said, “Ok, out there I can’t have you saving anybody’s butt when a lot more of the black goo monsters are chasing you.” Focusing on what she was saying, I put my guard down, so she grabbed me with the vine. Bruh.

entries.title: Day 30
entries.body:
“Bro, come on! Are you trying to act like my baby sister? Because both of you think you can stop me,” I said, trying to break free from the vine. It failed. I had this epic idea where I was going to say that and break free, then finally run forward starting a fight; but the vines had like supernatural strength. Also, when I moved, the vine glowed and tightened.
“No, I am not trying to stop you, nor trying to be like your sister, who I don’t know. But I am trying to keep you safe because I personally care about you and know more of this stuff than you do. I know what you are thinking. I am not a smart alec. I just know what you are thinking.”

entries.title: Day 31
entries.body:
Layla looked into my eyes while reciting her very detailed response, and for a little while after, said nothing. She was only trying to protect me from the danger I put myself into. Also, she seemed like a caring person, so I kept my cool and chose to listen. But she does have seriously pretty eyes.
“Thank you,” I said. This was weird, because normally I would not have listened, or I would be trying to persuade her to let me be. But something about her seemed to keep me content with being a little humble. I said nothing else in the moment.
“Ok, I want to ask you a question,” she finally said after staring into my soul for what felt like five minutes. “Have you seen me before?”
“No, why?”
“Oh, nothing.”

entries.title: Day 32
entries.body:
“Like actually, why did you ask me that?” I said.
“You ask a lot of questions, huh?”
“Answer my question,” I replied.
“I was assigned to spy on you.”
I looked at her to see if she was legit. She looked guilty; that meant I was being watched. Great! “Did you see me naked?” I asked.
“What? No!” Layla said in response to my random question, but then she changed the subject. “Alright, so I was assigned to protect you from the stuff you just saw and much more, and to collect information for my boss, who you probably guessed was Martin. Yes, I am watching you all the time, other than when you are sleeping or naked. Protocol.”

entries.title: Day 33
entries.body:
By this time, we had already exited the school and gone into an underground tunnel, since Layla must know everything about me and this place. But I don’t know—the hallway just kept going. It all did. Apparently, she was “my spy.”
“I am,” she said out of the blue.
“Ok?”
“Yes!” she said as she kept moving, her eyes still locked on me. Then she turned, and we went through the wall with me still in her grasp.
We entered a new room: a bedroom. It was a small room with a bed on one side, a foot away from the bed, and there was a closet with shirts similar to the one Layla was wearing. Below, there were stacks of bras, underwear, and shorts.
